title: Regression Detection Threshold Configuration
description: Schema for regression detection threshold configuration in the PROJ-036 Prompt Regression Test Harness. Regression thresholds govern the statistical comparison engine (Layer 4 of the Four-Layer Composite Architecture) that classifies score distribution shifts between prompt versions as NO_REGRESSION, MARGINAL, or REGRESSION.

agent.description: The agent this threshold configuration applies to, or 'all' for universal configuration.

version.description: Contract version for this threshold configuration.

wilcoxon.description: Wilcoxon signed-rank test configuration. Used for comparing score distributions between prompt version A (baseline) and version B (candidate).

regression_p_cutoff.description: P-value below which a score distribution difference is classified as statistically significant (required for REGRESSION classification, combined with effect size). Standard: 0.05.

marginal_p_cutoff.description: P-value below which a result is flagged as MARGINAL (possible regression requiring monitoring). Must be > regression_p_cutoff. Standard: 0.10.

no_regression_p_floor.description: P-value at or above which the null hypothesis (no difference) is accepted and NO_REGRESSION is declared. Must equal marginal_p_cutoff for consistency.

alternative_hypothesis.description: The alternative hypothesis for the Wilcoxon test. 'two-sided' detects any significant change (both regression and improvement). Recommended for regression testing to avoid missing regressions masked by concurrent improvements in other dimensions.

minimum_n_per_version.description: Minimum number of evaluation runs per prompt version required before Wilcoxon test is valid. Below this minimum, InsufficientSamplesError is raised and the evaluation is labeled INSUFFICIENT_SAMPLE. Per ADR-001 FM-002.

recommended_n_per_version.description: Recommended number of evaluation runs per prompt version to achieve 80% statistical power for detecting medium effects (Cohen's r = 0.30) at alpha = 0.05.

tie_handling.description: How tied ranks are handled in the Wilcoxon test. 'average' is the scipy default and is appropriate for bounded quality scores that may cluster at common values.

rationale.description: Rationale for the chosen Wilcoxon configuration, citing the statistical basis.
rationale.default: Wilcoxon signed-rank is distribution-free and appropriate for bounded [0,1] quality scores that may not be normally distributed. Per ADR-001 Force F-2 and ICML 2025 position paper: CLT-based methods perform poorly for small N LLM evaluation sets. Minimum N=20 per FM-002 mitigation.

wilson_score.description: Wilson score interval configuration for estimating the proportion of runs meeting the quality gate threshold (score >= 0.92).

confidence_level.description: Confidence level for the Wilson score interval. Must match 1 - alpha used in Wilcoxon test for consistency. Standard: 0.95.

pass_rate_threshold.description: Score threshold defining 'pass' for Wilson interval calculation. A run is counted as a pass if score >= this threshold. Must be 0.92 per quality-enforcement.md H-13.

minimum_n_for_reliable_interval.description: Minimum N below which Wilson intervals are too wide to be useful (interval width > maximum_acceptable_interval_width). Below this N, interval results are flagged INSUFFICIENT_SAMPLE.

maximum_acceptable_interval_width.description: Maximum acceptable Wilson interval width (upper_bound - lower_bound). Intervals wider than this value provide insufficient precision for go/no-go decisions. Standard: 0.30.

rate_regression_detection.description: Configuration for detecting RATE_REGRESSION via non-overlapping Wilson intervals.

enabled.description: Whether RATE_REGRESSION detection via Wilson interval comparison is enabled.

detection_criterion.description: Criterion for declaring RATE_REGRESSION: 'non_overlapping' means the intervals must be completely non-overlapping with the candidate interval being lower.

bonferroni.description: Bonferroni correction configuration for controlling family-wise error rate when comparing multiple metrics simultaneously.

base_alpha.description: Base significance level before correction. Standard: 0.05.

correction_method.description: Multiple testing correction method. 'bonferroni' applies the classical correction; 'holm' applies the less conservative Holm-Bonferroni step-down method.

comparison_sets.description: Defined sets of simultaneous comparisons with pre-computed corrected alpha levels.

description.description: Description of what metrics are compared in this set.

k_comparisons.description: Number of simultaneous comparisons in this set.

corrected_alpha.description: Bonferroni-corrected alpha = base_alpha / k_comparisons (or Holm-adjusted equivalent). Pre-computed for implementation reference.

recommended_for.description: Evaluation mode(s) where this comparison set is applied.

effect_size.description: Effect size (Cohen's r) thresholds for regression classification. Cohen's r is derived from Wilcoxon Z-statistic: r = Z / sqrt(N).

negligible_maximum.description: Maximum Cohen's r below which the effect is classified as negligible. Even statistically significant results with r < negligible_maximum are classified as NO_REGRESSION. Standard: 0.10.

small_maximum.description: Maximum Cohen's r for 'small' effect size. Results with r in [negligible_maximum, small_maximum) with p < regression_p_cutoff are classified as MARGINAL. Standard: 0.20.

medium_maximum.description: Maximum Cohen's r for 'medium' effect size. Results with r in [small_maximum, medium_maximum) may be MARGINAL or REGRESSION depending on p-value. Standard: 0.30.

regression_minimum.description: Minimum Cohen's r at which a statistically significant result (p < regression_p_cutoff) with mean_delta < 0 is classified as REGRESSION rather than MARGINAL. Standard: 0.30.

rationale.description: Rationale for the chosen effect size thresholds, citing Cohen (1988) conventions.
rationale.default: Cohen (1988) conventions: r=0.10 small, r=0.30 medium, r=0.50 large. The regression_minimum of 0.30 ensures that only medium-or-larger effects trigger REGRESSION classification, preventing false alarms from small score fluctuations that are within expected measurement noise. At N=30, a Wilcoxon test can detect r as small as 0.05, making the effect size filter essential.

evaluation_mode_thresholds.description: Mode-specific threshold configurations overriding defaults where applicable.

smoke.description: Smoke mode (N=1) configuration. Statistical testing is disabled; only structural invariants are checked.

standard.description: Standard mode (N=10) configuration. Statistical testing disabled (N < 20 minimum); simple quality check against agent floor. QUALITY_FLOOR_BREACH is intentionally excluded from Standard mode: it requires Wilson score intervals which need N >= 20. Standard mode uses QUALITY_CHECK_FAIL (mean-based) as the floor signal instead. Per-agent merge_decisions tables that list QUALITY_FLOOR_BREACH apply that classification only when the harness is running in Full mode.

statistical_testing_enabled.description: N=10 < 20 minimum for Wilcoxon; statistical testing is disabled in Standard mode.

mr_testing_enabled.description: Subset of MRs (MR-001, MR-004) is tested in Standard mode.

regression_classifications_available.description: Standard mode classifications. QUALITY_FLOOR_BREACH is absent by design: it requires Wilson intervals (N >= 20). QUALITY_CHECK_FAIL is the Standard-mode equivalent floor signal (mean-based, not interval-based).

simple_quality_check.description: Simple mean-based quality check replacing Wilcoxon in Standard mode.

full.description: Full mode (N=30) configuration. All statistical tests, all 5 MRs, full classification available.

regression_classification_rules.description: Ordered list of classification rules evaluated against Wilcoxon results. Rules are evaluated in order; the first matching rule determines the classification.

classification.description: Output classification if all conditions are met.

conditions.description: Conditions that must all be true (AND logic) for this rule to match.

merge_decision.description: Merge gate decision for this classification.

rationale.description: Explanation of why this rule produces this classification.

source.description: Reference to behavioral-contracts.md section defining these thresholds.

wilcoxon.rationale: Wilcoxon is distribution-free, robust to outliers, and appropriate for bounded [0,1] quality scores. Per ADR-001 FM-002 and ICML 2025 evidence.

comparison_sets.description: Full evaluation: 6 S-014 dimensions + 1 composite + 5 MRs + 1 pass rate = 13 comparisons (authoritative k value; field corrected_alpha_full_k13 in per-agent contracts references this set)

effect_size.rationale: Cohen (1988) conventions with r=0.10 as negligible-to-small boundary. r>=0.30 (medium) required to classify as REGRESSION to prevent false alarms at N=30.

regression_classification_rules.rationale: P >= 0.10: null hypothesis accepted; differences within expected random variation regardless of effect size.
Statistically significant but negligible effect (r < 0.10). At N=30, Wilcoxon detects differences as small as r=0.05. Below 0.10, practical significance is absent.
Statistically significant improvement. Log and allow merge; not a regression.
Borderline significance; possible regression. Allow merge with logged warning and monitoring.
Significant but small-to-medium effect. Not definitively regression-level; allow merge with warning.
Statistically significant medium-or-larger degradation. This is a regression; block merge.
